title: A Centralized Pathology Protocol for Global Cancer Genomics
author: Behnoush Abedi-Ardekani
materials: A. Frozen sectioning for pathology evaluation
Re-check that the case ID matches all materials.
Follow steps to embed and freeze
Follow steps 1-4 for reagent set up and 12-13 for equipment set up
Fix slide in 70% ethanol for 2 min.
Air-dry at room temperature for 5 min.
Proceed to step 10 of equipment setup.
Acquire images before and after microdissection.

steps.title: Retrieve frozen tissue cryotubes
steps.instruction: Remove the cryotubes containing frozen tissues from the deep freezer (–80 °C or –20 °C) according to the list provided by the data manager.

steps.title: Verify and label sample IDs
steps.instruction: Confirm the identification number of each cryotube and apply the unique ID to all equipment (glass slides, cryotubes, OCT blocks, etc.) using the institutional sample‑tracking system.

steps.title: Transfer cryotubes to cryostat chamber
steps.instruction: Carry the cryotubes in a cryobox on dry ice (long distance) or ice cubes (short distance) to the pathology laboratory, then transfer them from the cryobox into the pre‑cooled cryostat chamber (maintained at –20 °C). Allow the tubes to equilibrate for 1–2 min. Process only 1–2 cryotubes at a time; keep remaining tubes on dry ice with lid closed.

steps.title: Prepare cryomold with OCT base
steps.instruction: Select a cryomold slightly larger than the specimen, label it with the specimen ID using a cryo‑pen, pour a thin layer of OCT to cover the bottom, and let it opacify (not fully solidify) for 10–30 s to create a flat base.

steps.title: Place tissue in OCT and blot
steps.instruction: Using pre‑cooled forceps, remove the tissue from the cryotube and place it on the OCT base. For RNAlater®‑preserved tissue, gently blot with a Kimwipe until no visible liquid remains (do not wash with PBS). Press the tissue gently to ensure even attachment and no air pockets, then add OCT to fully cover the tissue while avoiding bubble formation.

steps.title: Infiltrate OCT and solidify block
steps.instruction: Leave the cryomold in the cryostat chamber undisturbed for 15–30 s to allow OCT infiltration and bubble dissipation, then transfer the cryomold to the freezing stage and allow the OCT to fully solidify for 20–50 s.

steps.title: Store OCT block if not sectioning
steps.instruction: If sectioning will not be performed immediately, store the OCT blocks at –80 °C (pause point).

steps.title: Mount OCT block on chuck and freeze
steps.instruction: Apply a small drop of fresh OCT onto the flat surface of the chuck, place the OCT block on it (OCT bedding), and put the chuck with the attached block in the pre‑cooled freezing stage. Allow it to freeze for about 5 min.

steps.title: Install new blade and set angle
steps.instruction: Slide a pre‑cooled disposable blade into the holder, adjust the angle, and secure it with the locking mechanism. Use a new blade for each tissue block and process one specimen at a time to prevent contamination.

steps.title: Set and trim section thickness
steps.instruction: Select tissue section thickness using the ‘+’ and ‘‑’ buttons. Trim the block at 20–30 µm until a flat tissue surface is exposed (slow trimming for small biopsies). Cut sections at 5 µm for histopathology assessment, 10 µm for flank sectioning, and 15 µm for laser capture microdissection (LCM).

steps.title: Mount sections onto Superfrost slides
steps.instruction: Mount each section onto a pre‑labeled, pre‑cooled Superfrost™ Plus slide (required for frozen tissues to prevent wash‑out).

steps.title: Air‑dry slides before fixation
steps.instruction: Leave the slides on the slide rack inside the cryostat. After all slides are prepared, remove the rack and allow the slides to air‑dry at room temperature for ≥10 min to prevent folding or cracking during staining.

steps.title: Fix sections in 4 % PFA
steps.instruction: Fix sections in freshly prepared 4 % paraformaldehyde for 10–15 min (perform in a laminar‑flow hood, Level 2 containment).

steps.title: Rinse slides briefly in PBS
steps.instruction: Briefly rinse the slides in PBS and drain excess liquid.

steps.title: Perform hematoxylin‑eosin staining sequence
steps.instruction: Stain sequentially: Hematoxylin 5 min, tap‑water rinse 5 min, Eosin 2–3 min, ethanol series (70 %, 95 %, 100 %; 1–2 changes each), xylene (2 changes, 5 min each). Do not rinse after eosin to avoid washing out the stain.

steps.title: Scan slides for whole‑slide imaging
steps.instruction: Proceed to scanning and whole‑slide image (WSI) creation for downstream analysis (Part 2).

steps.title: Adjust thickness for LCM
steps.instruction: Change the section thickness to 15 µm (avoid >15 µm as laser cutting becomes inefficient). Ensure a flat, wrinkle‑free section centered on the membrane with a 1.5 cm margin; discard any folded sections.

steps.title: Store unfixed LCM slides at –80 °C
steps.instruction: If LCM will not be performed immediately, store the unfixed slides at –80 °C (pause point).

steps.title: Open image viewer and data registry
steps.instruction: Open the SlidePath image viewer (replacing Aperio Image Scope) and the pathology data registry program according to institutional setup.

steps.title: Determine workflow option based on pathology data
steps.instruction: Review tumor type, PVTC, and surface size to select an option:

substeps.instruction: If non‑malignant tissue, extensive necrosis, or non‑eligible cancer type → Option A.
If eligible cancer type and PVTC ≥ 50 % → Option B.
If eligible cancer type and PVTC ≈ 1 mm² → Option C.
If pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with PVTC < 50 % → Option D.
If eligible cancer type, PVTC ≥ 50 % but surface ≤ 1 mm² → Option E.

steps.title: Annotate area of interest
steps.instruction: Annotate the area of interest on the slide (for macrodissection or LCM) using the software drawing tool.

steps.title: Verify case list and extract OCT block
steps.instruction: Verify the case list prepared by the data manager, then extract the OCT block from –80 °C storage and check the case ID.

steps.title: Transfer and equilibrate OCT block in cryostat
steps.instruction: Transfer the OCT block to the pre‑cooled cryostat chamber and equilibrate in the freezing stage for 10–15 min.

steps.title: Align annotations on OCT block
steps.instruction: Examine corresponding glass slides and WSIs, orient the pathologist’s annotations on the OCT block, and keep images and slides visible for reference.

steps.title: Trim OCT block with disposable scalpel
steps.instruction: Apply a new disposable scalpel and make shallow cuts to remove unwanted areas, placing the OCT block on a solid, even surface (use forceps, not hands). After delineation, deepen the cuts.

steps.title: Thaw dissected block and place in new cryomold
steps.instruction: Allow the dissected OCT block to slightly thaw, remove it, and place it on a clean cryomold. Identify the post‑macro OCT block according to institutional tracking.

steps.title: Store post‑macro block if needed
steps.instruction: If not immediately sectioned, store the post‑macro OCT block at –80 °C (pause point). Discard the disposable scalpel in a sharps container.

steps.title: Identify slide ID and dip in cresyl violet
steps.instruction: Check the slide ID against the list provided by the data manager, then dip the slide for 10 s in 1 % cresyl violet acetate working solution.

steps.title: Load slide and collection tube for LCM
steps.instruction: Load the stained slide into the slide holder and load an adhesive cap collection tube (500 µL).

steps.title: Annotate regions and execute laser capture
steps.instruction: Follow pathologist guidance to annotate regions of interest, then start the laser beam to cut and catapult material into the cap. Calibrate the laser, align the tube, avoid air currents, check alignment regularly, scan the slide at the end to confirm collection, and apply additional laser power if needed.

steps.title: Seal and store collected material at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Remove the collection tube, close, seal, label, and store it at –20 °C until DNA extraction.

steps.title: UV‑crosslink or use certified PEN slides
steps.instruction: UV‑crosslink PEN slides for 30 min, or use certified DNase/RNase‑free PEN slides as done in the institute.

steps.title: Use new scalpel for each sample
steps.instruction: Use a new scalpel for each sample to avoid DNA contamination.
